title: BCG vaccine as an encyclopedia object
dek: Calmette and Guérin, daughter strains, childhood meningitis protection. RD1 genetics stay on tb-bcg-rd1; this card is the vaccine node.
story: Wikipedia's BCG vaccine page (Q798309; the Bacillus Calmette–Guérin title redirects here) is a public-health node: a live M. bovis derivative, given to neonates in many programmes, better at preventing childhood miliary disease and meningitis than adult cavities.

Daughter strains (Pasteur, Danish, Tokyo, Russia, Moreau) are a Wikipedia graph of extra RD losses. That graph is why a single RD PCR is not a full strain ID — the genetics plate already said so; this card names the strains as encyclopedia objects.
Efficacy-by-latitude stories, NTM sensitisation, and bladder instillation for urothelial carcinoma all live on the page. None of them is TPT. None of them is a four-drug backbone.
deepTitle: What this node must not steal from WHO
deep: Contraindications in untreated advanced HIV and MSMD are clinical policy. Follow WHO/national EPI sheets, not the talk page.
BCG-osis is an immunodeficiency until proven otherwise — same sentence as tb-bcg-rd1, linked rather than restated as a protocol.
New subunit vaccines (M72/AS01E and others) are not BCG. Keep them off this node.
TST cross-reactivity is why IGRAs exist. That hand-off goes to wiki-igra-glossary and tb-igra-tst.

example.title: Adult cavity after childhood BCG
example.setup: A 34-year-old with a cavity, neonatal BCG scar, IGRA positive, Ultra MTB detected.

steps.title: BCG did not fail a promise it did not make
steps.body: Adult cavitary protection is the weak job on the encyclopedia node.

steps.title: Scar is not a DST
steps.body: Treat the Ultra and the culture.

steps.title: Do not skip TPT debates in contacts because 'everyone is vaccinated'
steps.body: TPT is a different Wikipedia-adjacent object and a different WHO module.

example.takeaway: BCG is a named vaccine node, not sterilizing immunity.
